repair1.prompt_addition: 4. The repository to fix is checked out at /testbed, which is the working directory for every action. It is installed in editable (development) mode in the active Python environment, so importing the package runs the code in /testbed and your edits there take effect immediately. repair1.inserted_after: However, you can prefix any action with `MY_ENV_VAR=MY_VALUE cd /path/to/working/dir && ...` or write/load environment variables from files
repair1.stall_rule: A turn is recorded only when the agent executed exactly one action: (normalized command, return code, output fingerprint); normalized command = the command stripped with whitespace runs collapsed to one space; output fingerprint = sha256 of the output with whitespace runs collapsed to one space and stripped, then two volatile token kinds masked (Python re): hexadecimal literals 0x[0-9a-fA-F]+ (per-process object addresses, e.g. in pip retry warnings) -> 0x_ and decimal-second durations \b[0-9]+\.[0-9]+s\b (e.g. pytest 'in 3.21s') -> _s. A FormatError turn or a turn with a number of actions other than one is recorded as a chain reset. Before each model query, before the frozen limit checks and before n_calls is incremented: if the last two recorded turns are equal and their return code is nonzero, raise RepeatedFailureStall carrying the exit message; the frozen run() records it as the exit with an empty submission. No model call, nothing shown to the model.

declared_rules: Task exposure: astropy__astropy-14598 is already DEVELOPMENT-exposed (REQ-011) and may never enter CONFIRM. The probe is a mechanism check on this one exposed issue. The lead chose it from observed data (the 7B's first REQ-011 call reproduced the bug), so it is not confirmatory selection, a success rate or a routing contrast.

Configuration yaml-v1-repair1 (new, versioned, DEVELOPMENT) is the frozen yaml-v1 configuration with exactly three changes: (i) the instance template gets repair1.prompt_addition as item 4 at the end of its '## Important Rules' list, inserted after repair1.inserted_after (exact bytes and sha256 before and after in prompt_bytes; no solution content); (ii) the agent container run_args are repair1.run_args (--network none: no egress); (iii) the agent class is repair1.agent_class, a subclass of the unmodified DefaultAgent that adds only the stall guard. Every other setting is the REQ-011 one, as are the model request path, the receipts, the Submitted-only wc2 endpoint, the all-exit diagnostic and cleanup. No cue, no forced call, no salvage, no substitution, no endpoint or metric change, no second model, task or cohort.

Runtime overrides (declared; req012_entry.py, in the entry process only). They are installed after the REQ-011-style admission of the running code and before cue_episode.run_episode (unchanged) builds anything: (a) pilot_episode.build_effective_config is wrapped so its result passes through repair_config; (b) minisweagent.agents.default.DefaultAgent is set to the guard subclass, which run_episode imports at call time. No source file is edited. entry_admitted.json records the overrides and the entry source sha256. After the episode, repair_record.json records the guard's turns and whether effective_config.json equals the expected repair1 config; a mismatch is reported in the summary, never repaired. Before the first query the guard records the episode container's docker NetworkMode once (observational).

Stall guard (observational; RepeatedFailureStall): repair1.stall_rule. The exit message is exactly repair1.stall_exit_message. It saves calls only after two identical failing turns, makes no model call, shows nothing to the model and never produces a submission; the all-exit diagnostic, the receipts and cleanup run as on every exit.

No-model repair gate (req012_pair.py --gate; no model, no llama-server, no request). gate.preflight runs first and a refusal there creates no namespace. Then, in gate.order with short-circuiting, the manifest, sources, fixtures and image checks run, and one repair1 agent container runs gate.commands G0-G7 through the unmodified DockerEnvironment.execute with the frozen 60 s command timeout. Each command is recorded as (command, rc, output sha256, bounded excerpt); then the container is stopped and removed. The gate passes only if gate.passes_only_if holds. The record results/v2_agent/req012_repair_probe_20260924/gate.json is write-once and sanitized, with a raw copy under work/. It records the preflight, the manifest sha256, the repair1 prompt bytes, both template texts, the effective environment, the digest of every source and any operator signal (gate.interruption). The gate is single-shot (a second --gate refuses) and is part of this namespace. G0 (pwd) is a declared addition to the lead's G1-G7, checking that /testbed is the working directory the prompt states. gate.egress_evidence states what the fixtures do and do not show.

Gate revisions before the first --gate run (review of the uncommitted build; no gate had run). (1) G1: the pinned instance image's HEAD is not the dataset base_commit. SWE-bench's image setup pins setuptools in pyproject.toml and runs `git commit --allow-empty -am SWE-bench`, so HEAD is gate.image_head, whose parent is the base commit (gate.image_head_evidence). G1 therefore checks HEAD, HEAD^, the HEAD subject, the files HEAD changes and a clean status. (2) G5: offline, pip finds no index candidate and may keep the installed editable astropy ('Requirement already satisfied', rc 0). No rc is required; the check is that nothing was installed and the checkout path, version and editable location are unchanged afterwards (G5_then_G2, G5_then_G3). (3) The gate arms signal handling, refuses before its namespace on a failed preflight, and short-circuits before the container after a failed check. These revisions make the checks match the pinned image; they do not change the lead's acceptance criteria.

Probe precondition: the probe refuses before creating anything unless the published gate.json passed for this manifest sha256 and for the current digest of every source, and the raw copy under work/ agrees with it on passed, interrupted, manifest sha256, source digests and start/finish times. The same check is repeated as an admission probe.

Queue: exactly one assignment, req012-1-small: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B ('small', port 8291, the 87a3665c GGUF), arm 'baseline', on astropy__astropy-14598 under yaml-v1-repair1. No automatic second model, task or cohort.

Single shot: work/runs/req012_repair_probe_20260924/probe and results/v2_agent/req012_repair_probe_20260924/probe are created with exist_ok=False at launch, so a second launch refuses. A started assignment is never re-dispatched, and a start without an end in the ledger is 'interrupted'. A BLOCKED admission also consumes the probe namespace.

Admission (any failure or crashing probe -> admission.json and pair_summary.json with status BLOCKED; nothing is run and nothing is substituted) consists of the REQ-011 probes plus a passing gate record. The REQ-011 probes are: manifest values bound to the code, including the repair1 prompt bytes from the pinned default.yaml; every reused and new source tracked and unchanged from HEAD, and the cue-v1 binding without problems; the evaluator tree; the colima runtime; the three image pins; conflicts, including the live peer lease and windows, the ownership record, no REQ-011 or REQ-012 PAUSE file and no other REQ-011 or REQ-012 process; isolation, where the repair1 environment must have run_args exactly --rm --platform linux/amd64 --network none and otherwise meet the REQ-011 sandbox rule; disk; the 7B GGUF and llama.cpp tool hashes; memory.

Memory, disk, serving, served identity and the watchdog are as in REQ-011: req011_pair.probe_memory and probe_disk; Servers with the ownership holder rewritten to DTR-REQ-012; GET-only served-identity checks; 0 non-task generation requests; the watchdog is started before the load and left armed while a server of ours is live.

Schedule (3600 s): the probe deadline is launch time + caps.pair_wall_s. It covers admission, load, the episode, grading, cleanup and publication. The episode starts only if now + episode_load_allowance_s (300) + episode_wall_s (1800) + child_cleanup_grace_s (120) + child_wait_slack_s (30) + server_cleanup_reserve_s (90) <= deadline - grading_floor_s (900). This is re-checked after the load with a zero load allowance; otherwise the episode is 'not_started: pair cap'. The episode's block deadline is deadline - grading_floor_s. The grading floor is evaluator_min_start_budget_s (600) + evaluator_end_reserve_s (300), so an episode admitted by the post-load check leaves the first evaluator attempt its 600 s start budget even at the full 1800 s episode wall. The pre-load allowance of 300 s is 100 times the 7B's REQ-011 hash plus load time (3.1 s) and only gates the dispatch; the post-load check with zero allowance still enforces the full budget. The worker specification's 600 s floor was inconsistent with the unchanged evaluator start rule and was corrected before the gate.

Gates that stop the probe are as in REQ-011 and never outcome-driven: a server load failure or refusal, served identity, post-load memory, the PAUSE file, an entry refusal, a record not written durably, and unconfirmed process-group termination or container removal.

Episode supervision is as in REQ-011 (req011_pair.make_episode_runner), with req012_entry.py as the child. The entry refuses unless its control record matches this manifest (binding sha256; instance; expected image; assignment id, order, backend, port, alias and model sha256; the repair1 prompt bytes) and the request limit is min(48, 48 - counted_before).

Request accounting: at most 24 logical calls (the frozen step limit) and at most 48 physical requests (2 attempts per call). counted_before is 0 and the request limit is 48. Unknown or invalid counts reserve 48 (cue_admission.account_requests). No non-task generation request is sent.

Grading is as in REQ-011: req011_grade.py unchanged, grade_identity.grade_flow, the stock f7bbbb2 evaluator and strict declared_outcome. It runs after the server is stopped, in a fresh evaluator container created by the stock harness from the pinned instance image; the image ID must equal the pin before and after grading, and the agent container is never used. Each evaluator attempt has a wall budget of min(1800, deadline - 300 - now) and starts only if that budget is >= 600 s; otherwise the record is 'ungraded: pair cap' (never imputed). One identical retry is allowed only after a stock timeout, a wall kill, or test output without a report.

Outcome rule: RepeatedFailureStall, LimitsExceeded, any other non-Submitted exit and a Submitted empty patch are operational zeros; grade_flow writes them without the evaluator. Only a Submitted nonempty submission.diff is graded.

Publication is as in REQ-011 (req011_pair.publish: sanitized copies with raw and published sha256, and the username guard), under results/v2_agent/req012_repair_probe_20260924/probe. Private raw request bodies stay under outputs.private_receipts/<run_id>.

Summary (pair_summary.json): the REQ-011 assignment row, with outcome_source 'stall_guard' for a completed episode whose exit is RepeatedFailureStall. It adds per row the repair1 facts: whether the guard fired and before which logical call, the docker NetworkMode observed, the run_args at container start, the effective-config verification, the effective-config and instance-template sha256, and the agent class. It also adds the manifest prompt bytes and the prior results: the REQ-011 pair_summary and yaml-v1 block report sha256 unchanged, and REQ-011 eligible 0 of 2.

Interpretation (lead decision): this is a mechanism check, not success-rate evidence. An eligible nonempty patch graded by the unchanged evaluator would show single-task feasibility of the repair1 intervention and nothing more. Another zero would localize the remaining failure from the saved actions and edits. Either way the earlier 0/32 and 0/2 results are reported unchanged, and the worker returns to the lead before any expansion.

interpretations.nonblocking: The all-exit diagnostic, post-dispatch receipt bookkeeping and cleanup never change the endpoint, eligibility or grading and never stop the pair. The PRE-dispatch receipt stays blocking (no dispatch without a durable receipt) per the lead's REQ-005 decision (answer 1); the disk reserve for it is checked at admission.
interpretations.probe_cap: Time expiry preserves and publishes incomplete work with its reason; no extra time, outcome-driven stopping or substitution.
interpretations.gate: The gate verifies the environment and the harness only. It sends no model request and is not evidence about model competence.
